blocks.text: The gift is knowledge of the Self.
blocks.directed: The gift is knowledge of the Self.

blocks.text: The Greatest Gift Isn’t Money. It’s Helping Somebody Realise What They Actually Are.
blocks.directed: The Greatest Gift Isn’t Money. It’s Helping Somebody Realise What They Actually Are.

blocks.text: Because after all the metaphysics, after the entire cosmic theatre, after the extraordinary powers and the subtle bodies and the phonemic goddesses, Vasugupta arrives at something profoundly human.
blocks.directed: Because after all the metaphysics, after the entire cosmic theatre, after the extraordinary powers and the subtle bodies and the phonemic goddesses, Vasugupta arrives at something profoundly human.

blocks.text: And what does the realised yogi give?
blocks.directed: And what does the realised yogi give?

blocks.text: The gift is knowledge of the Self.
blocks.directed: The gift is knowledge of the Self.

blocks.text: Now think about the ordinary understanding of generosity.
blocks.directed: Now think about the ordinary understanding of generosity.

blocks.text: All of these can be valuable.
blocks.directed: All of these can be valuable.

blocks.text: But within the liberation-centred framework of Trika, there is something more fundamental that can be communicated.
blocks.directed: But within the liberation-centred framework of Trika, there is something more fundamental that can be communicated.

blocks.text: And Kṣemarāja explicitly interprets this sūtra through the relationship between teacher and disciple.
blocks.directed: And Kṣemarāja explicitly interprets this sūtra through the relationship between teacher and disciple.

blocks.text: The realised yogi imparts knowledge of the Self to students.
blocks.directed: The realised yogi imparts knowledge of the Self to students.

blocks.text: Not simply information about a philosophical doctrine.
blocks.directed: Not simply information about a philosophical doctrine.

blocks.text: But the liberating recognition of consciousness.
blocks.directed: But the liberating recognition of consciousness.

blocks.text: And here’s where Kṣemarāja gives us a fascinating little Sanskrit discussion.
blocks.directed: And here’s where Kṣemarāja gives us a fascinating little Sanskrit discussion.

blocks.text: He explores the word dāna through several traditional verbal associations.
blocks.directed: He explores the word dāna through several traditional verbal associations.

blocks.text: Now, these shouldn’t all be treated as the ordinary historical derivation of dāna.
blocks.directed: Now, these shouldn’t all be treated as the ordinary historical derivation of dāna.

blocks.text: Rather, Kṣemarāja is using a traditional style of exegetical wordplay to disclose different dimensions of the teaching.
blocks.directed: Rather, Kṣemarāja is using a traditional style of exegetical wordplay to disclose different dimensions of the teaching.

blocks.text: That knowledge cuts through the apparent separation between Śiva and the universe.
blocks.directed: That knowledge cuts through the apparent separation between Śiva and the universe.

blocks.text: It purifies the limitations associated with Māyā.
blocks.directed: It purifies the limitations associated with Māyā.

blocks.text: And it helps preserve the recognition of the supreme reality.
blocks.directed: And it helps preserve the recognition of the supreme reality.

blocks.text: But then Kṣemarāja returns to the central meaning.
blocks.directed: But then Kṣemarāja returns to the central meaning.

blocks.text: The realised yogi gives Self-knowledge to disciples.
blocks.directed: The realised yogi gives Self-knowledge to disciples.

blocks.text: And he explicitly uses a word associated with students dwelling near the teacher.
blocks.directed: And he explicitly uses a word associated with students dwelling near the teacher.

blocks.text: Somebody living in proximity to the teacher.
blocks.directed: Somebody living in proximity to the teacher.

blocks.text: This is a reminder that we’re dealing with a historical tradition of instruction and transmission, not simply an abstract theory of consciousness.
blocks.directed: This is a reminder that we’re dealing with a historical tradition of instruction and transmission, not simply an abstract theory of consciousness.

blocks.text: He cites a traditional claim that accomplished yogis established in the unity of Śiva, Śakti and the individual can liberate others through their presence or touch.
blocks.directed: He cites a traditional claim that accomplished yogis established in the unity of Śiva, Śakti and the individual can liberate others through their presence or touch.

blocks.text: This is a claim about divine grace and the extraordinary efficacy of realised teachers within the tantric tradition.
blocks.directed: This is a claim about divine grace and the extraordinary efficacy of realised teachers within the tantric tradition.

blocks.text: It should not be presented as an experimentally established capacity to confer liberation by physical contact. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.
blocks.directed: It should not be presented as an experimentally established capacity to confer liberation by physical contact. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.

blocks.text: But philosophically, it tells us something profound about the ideal teacher.
blocks.directed: But philosophically, it tells us something profound about the ideal teacher.

blocks.text: The teacher isn’t merely someone who knows more facts than the pupil.
blocks.directed: The teacher isn’t merely someone who knows more facts than the pupil.

blocks.text: They’re someone whose recognition of the supreme reality can become an occasion for awakening in another.
blocks.directed: They’re someone whose recognition of the supreme reality can become an occasion for awakening in another.

blocks.text: And now think about the relationship between this sūtra and the previous one.
blocks.directed: And now think about the relationship between this sūtra and the previous one.

blocks.text: Speech has become rooted in recognition.
blocks.directed: Speech has become rooted in recognition.

blocks.text: And now speech can become an instrument through which recognition is communicated.
blocks.directed: And now speech can become an instrument through which recognition is communicated.

blocks.text: The very language that once contributed to bondage can become a vehicle of liberation.
blocks.directed: The very language that once contributed to bondage can become a vehicle of liberation.

blocks.text: The same power whose differentiated activity could conceal consciousness can now communicate knowledge of its source.
blocks.directed: The same power whose differentiated activity could conceal consciousness can now communicate knowledge of its source.

blocks.text: And therefore the teacher’s speech participates in the liberating function of Śakti.
blocks.directed: And therefore the teacher’s speech participates in the liberating function of Śakti.

blocks.text: Now, this is where Trika’s understanding of anugraha becomes important.
blocks.directed: Now, this is where Trika’s understanding of anugraha becomes important.

blocks.text: The power through which the supreme reality becomes recognised.
blocks.directed: The power through which the supreme reality becomes recognised.

blocks.text: In the broader Śaiva system, anugraha is one of the divine functions associated with Śiva.
blocks.directed: In the broader Śaiva system, anugraha is one of the divine functions associated with Śiva.

blocks.text: And the last is especially significant.
blocks.directed: And the last is especially significant.

blocks.text: Because the same supreme reality that freely permits contraction also possesses the power through which that contraction can be overcome.
blocks.directed: Because the same supreme reality that freely permits contraction also possesses the power through which that contraction can be overcome.

blocks.text: Within the tradition, the genuine teacher can function as a vehicle of that grace.
blocks.directed: Within the tradition, the genuine teacher can function as a vehicle of that grace.

blocks.text: The highest gift is not necessarily a new object added to the recipient’s possessions.
blocks.directed: The highest gift is not necessarily a new object added to the recipient’s possessions.

blocks.text: It is the disclosure of what was already fundamental.
blocks.directed: It is the disclosure of what was already fundamental.

blocks.text: Imagine somebody convinced they’ve lost their home.
blocks.directed: Imagine somebody convinced they’ve lost their home.
[short pause] And eventually somebody tells them:

blocks.text: The gift wasn’t a newly constructed house.
blocks.directed: The gift wasn’t a newly constructed house.

blocks.text: It was the recognition of their actual situation.
blocks.directed: It was the recognition of their actual situation.

blocks.text: But it captures the structure of pratyabhijñā.
blocks.directed: But it captures the structure of pratyabhijñā.

blocks.text: The teacher does not manufacture the student’s Self.
blocks.directed: The teacher does not manufacture the student’s Self.

blocks.text: And perhaps that is why this sūtra is so beautiful.
blocks.directed: And perhaps that is why this sūtra is so beautiful.

blocks.text: It takes the most extraordinary metaphysical doctrine imaginable and expresses its highest communicative function through a very ordinary human act.
blocks.directed: It takes the most extraordinary metaphysical doctrine imaginable and expresses its highest communicative function through a very ordinary human act.

blocks.text: And the knowledge is of the Self.
blocks.directed: And the knowledge is of the Self.

blocks.text: But now Vasugupta makes an important distinction.
blocks.directed: But now Vasugupta makes an important distinction.

blocks.text: Because not everybody who speaks about Śiva is necessarily capable of awakening others.
blocks.directed: Because not everybody who speaks about Śiva is necessarily capable of awakening others.

blocks.text: And the next sūtra is perhaps the most linguistically peculiar in the entire section.
blocks.directed: And the next sūtra is perhaps the most linguistically peculiar in the entire section.

blocks.text: Even Kṣemarāja has to deal with some rather adventurous etymological interpretations.
blocks.directed: Even Kṣemarāja has to deal with some rather adventurous etymological interpretations.

blocks.text: The man is apparently about to explain why people can get so carried away with Sanskrit wordplay that they start inventing entire philosophies out of syllables.
